standard_prerequisites.name: The sheaf of meromorphic functions is described locally on affine opens as quotients of a section by a nonzerodivisor, and the structure sheaf embeds into it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 6248-6252 and again at 6255-6257
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows writing the meromorphic function locally as a quotient and lets a section of the structure sheaf be viewed inside the meromorphic sheaf.

standard_prerequisites.name: On an affine scheme, killing a section after inverting an element is equivalent to annihilating it by a power of that element
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts vanishing of the image in the localization into the annihilation statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-compactness reduces a global statement to finitely many affine pieces
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof replace the scheme by one affine open on which the meromorphic function has the described form.

core_obligations: Reduce to a manageable cover: cover the quasi-compact scheme by finitely many affine opens on each of which the meromorphic function is a quotient of a section by a nonzerodivisor, so that it suffices to treat one such affine piece with the function written as such a quotient (proof lines 6248-6252).

Discard the denominator: since the denominator is a nonzerodivisor on the affine piece it suffices to prove the statement for the numerator, which is an honest section of the structure sheaf (proof lines 6252-6255).

Conclude: the hypothesis that the function restricts to zero on the principal open means that the numerator maps to zero in the localization, which on an affine scheme says exactly that a power of the defining element annihilates it (proof lines 6255-6258).
proof_roadmap: Cover by finitely many affine pieces and reduce to a meromorphic function written as a quotient on one of them (proof lines 6248-6252).
Use that the denominator is a nonzerodivisor to reduce to a section of the structure sheaf, and read annihilation off the localization (proof lines 6252-6258).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a quasi-compact scheme, a meromorphic function whose restriction to the principal open defined by a section h vanishes is annihilated by a power of h (statement lines 6241-6246). The counted proof reduces the statement to finitely many affine opens on which the meromorphic function is a quotient of a section by a nonzerodivisor, discards the denominator using that it is a nonzerodivisor, and then reads the annihilation statement off the fact that vanishing in a localization means being killed by a power of the inverted element (proof lines 6248-6258). It is H2: the reductions and the final step are carried out in the counted span and use only the local description of meromorphic functions.
